SL-73 grouped-call debt has a strict diagnostic comparison mode, with no tolerated-divergence ledger. This patch changes prototype sources, harnesses and documentation only; it adds no parser grammar or production compiler behavior.\n\nValidation: 15 focused canonical cases passed across VM, LLVM O0/O2, ASan and production sawc, with identical complete output. Nine also matched Python's parse-only oracle; the remaining cases use independent expected output for depth, renderer refusal and known grammar debt. Separate arena invariants passed. All 58 current candidates matched Python's canonical bytes under the VM, including 29 semantic-negative examples. The 35 combined Python harness tests and inventory snapshot freshness check passed. The snapshot uses a lossless column/string-table encoding to fit the tracker request limit; a full-corpus round-trip test verifies that it preserves every rich inventory record.\n\nCoverage is partial: 2,536 examples use unsupported syntax, 95 produce Python parse errors, and 7 remain unresolved. They are inventoried but do not count as parser agreement. The comparison deliberately reclassifies the current corpus on each run; snapshot freshness is a separate check. Design: prototypes/minivm/M19_PARSER_DIFFERENTIAL.md. This next\nincrement adds a Saw canonical renderer and a reproducible inventory of the\nexamples corpus. It does not expand the grammar or change the production\ncompiler. Work starts stacked on M18; submission must identify that dependency.\n\n## Canonical renderer\n\nAdd `prototypes/parser/src/canonical.saw`, assembled after the lexer and\nparser. Public entry: `canonical_ast(tree: &AstTree) -> Result<String, AstError>`.\nThe input contract is a tree returned by `parse_ast`; arbitrary fabricated\narenas are not a serialization format. Return a complete string or a located\nerror, never partial output presented as success.\n\nMatch the parse-only `sawc/ast_dump.py` byte format (without IDs, typechecking,\nstdlib, or trailing newline). `tools/dump_ast.py` adds one CLI newline; the\ncomparison adapter removes exactly that one byte. Preserve embedded newlines,\nNUL, Unicode, and spaces in string payloads. The current StringLiteral writer\nescapes double quotes only; do not substitute JSON escaping.\n\nUse an explicit traversal/action stack, so valid depth-256 trees and long\nshallow expression chains do not consume recursive VM call frames. Named\nenums describe action kinds. Emit one shared indentation/line funnel.\n\nProgram emits `Program {`, an optional `functions: [` list, and closing lines.\nFunction emits ordered inline `name: Type` parameters and return type, braces,\nthen its block contents. Parameter/NamedType/Block are structural, not standalone\ncanonical headers. Let and Var both emit LetStatement with the mutability word\nand optional annotation. Return, ExpressionStatement, FinalExpression map to\nReturnStatement, ExpressionStatement, and `final_expr:` respectively. Binary\nchildren use `left:` and `right:`; Unary has a single indented operand.\nIdentifier, BooleanLiteral and string literals follow their Python arms exactly.\n\nIntegerLiteral text retains normalized base notation plus suffix in M18.\nCanonical IntLiteral uses the mathematical decimal value and the fixed `: Int`\nlabel, as the existing dumper does. Strip only recognized suffixes; convert\nbase 2/8/16 to decimal with digit arithmetic rather than a machine-sized Int\naccumulator. Test UInt64's maximum (beyond signed Int), each radix, and suffixes.\nThe unchanged lexer bounds admitted integer magnitudes; this milestone does\nnot expand those bounds. This is rendering, not range/type checking; preserve\nthe original AST text.\n\nA Call whose callee is Identifier emits `FunctionCall name()` and ordered\n`arg[i]: ` labels, including the existing trailing space. The canonical schema\ncannot represent an arbitrary callee expression: return a located renderer\nerror for other callee kinds. Do not flatten, discard, or invent a schema for\nthem. Grouped identifier calls still have Identifier callees and can render;\nPython's misparse of that syntax remains a differential failure (SL-73), not a\npermission to copy the bug. This restriction belongs to the renderer, not the\nparser grammar.\n\n## Comparison and classification\n\nKeep canonical fixtures separate from M18's arena oracle. Author exact expected\ncanonical bytes for every supported node and formatting boundary; compare Saw\noutput under VM, LLVM O0/O2, ASan and production-sawc execution. Independently\ninvoke the Python parse-only oracle on fixtures within its correct grammar.\nKeep debt probes explicit and failing in a diagnostic comparison mode; never\nintroduce a known-divergence ledger or count debt as agreement.\n\nInventory every tracked `examples/**/*.saw` file, reporting top-level and\nnested counts separately. Use sorted repository-relative paths and source\nhashes, with no execution or typechecking of examples. Semantic EXPECT-error\ndirectives do not decide parser eligibility. Record parser verdict, supported\nsyntax evidence, unsupported features, oracle failures and unresolved cases\nseparately. A Python AST whitelist alone cannot establish eligibility: it may\nhave discarded syntax (SL-73), and metadata such as modifiers must be checked.\nThe classification must not use the prototype's rejection to justify exclusion.\n\nRun admitted examples through the Saw parser and canonical renderer using\nbounded embedded-source batches (the VM has no file-reading API). Any unexpected\nrefusal, mismatch, timeout, crash or malformed protocol record is a failure.\nPreserve source, both outputs, commands and diagnostics. Report the total census\nand compared count explicitly; never call a partial sweep full parser parity.\nUnknown classification stays visible and cannot silently become supported or\nexcluded. New examples must be reclassified rather than inherited by filename.\n\n## Work and validation\n\nThe parent authors the design and reviews integrations. Sol source agent owns\nthe renderer; Sol harness agent owns canonical fixtures/harness; a separate\nSol agent owns census/classification. Use isolated worktrees. Serialize compiler\ngates with the machine-wide suite lock. Focused Python tests cover classification\ndrift, semantic-negative eligibility, failure reporting and byte preservation.\nNo production compiler edits are included. File new production findings in\nsawtracker, checking existing issues first.\n\nThe first checkpoint is the renderer and measured inventory. Any ambiguous\ngrammar classification is reported for review before a comparison scope is\nfrozen. Parameter/NamedType/Block are structural, not standalone\\n+canonical headers. Let and Var both emit LetStatement with the mutability word\\n+and optional annotation. Return, ExpressionStatement, FinalExpression map to\\n+ReturnStatement, ExpressionStatement, and `final_expr:` respectively. Binary\\n+children use `left:` and `right:`; Unary has a single indented operand.\\n+Identifier, BooleanLiteral and string literals follow their Python arms exactly.\\n+\\n+IntegerLiteral text retains normalized base notation plus suffix in M18.\\n+Canonical IntLiteral uses the mathematical decimal value and the fixed `: Int`\\n+label, as the existing dumper does. Test UInt64's maximum (beyond signed Int), each radix, and suffixes.\\n+The unchanged lexer bounds admitted integer magnitudes; this milestone does\\n+not expand those bounds. This is rendering, not range/type checking; preserve\\n+the original AST text.\\n+\\n+A Call whose callee is Identifier emits `FunctionCall name()` and ordered\\n+`arg[i]: ` labels, including the existing trailing space. The canonical schema\\n+cannot represent an arbitrary callee expression: return a located renderer\\n+error for other callee kinds. Do not flatten, discard, or invent a schema for\\n+them. Grouped identifier calls still have Identifier callees and can render;\\n+Python's misparse of that syntax remains a differential failure (SL-73), not a\\n+permission to copy the bug. This restriction belongs to the renderer, not the\\n+parser grammar.\\n+\\n+## Comparison and classification\\n+\\n+Keep canonical fixtures separate from M18's arena oracle. Author exact expected\\n+canonical bytes for every supported node and formatting boundary; compare Saw\\n+output under VM, LLVM O0/O2, ASan and production-sawc execution. Independently\\n+invoke the Python parse-only oracle on fixtures within its correct grammar.\\n+Keep debt probes explicit and failing in a diagnostic comparison mode; never\\n+introduce a known-divergence ledger or count debt as agreement.\\n+\\n+Inventory every tracked `examples/**/*.saw` file, reporting top-level and\\n+nested counts separately. Use sorted repository-relative paths and source\\n+hashes, with no execution or typechecking of examples. Semantic EXPECT-error\\n+directives do not decide parser eligibility. Record parser verdict, supported\\n+syntax evidence, unsupported features, oracle failures and unresolved cases\\n+separately. A Python AST whitelist alone cannot establish eligibility: it may\\n+have discarded syntax (SL-73), and metadata such as modifiers must be checked.\\n+The classification must not use the prototype's rejection to justify exclusion.\\n+\\n+Run admitted examples through the Saw parser and canonical renderer using\\n+bounded embedded-source batches (the VM has no file-reading API). Any unexpected\\n+refusal, mismatch, timeout, crash or malformed protocol record is a failure.\\n+Preserve source, both outputs, commands and diagnostics. Report the total census\\n+and compared count explicitly; never call a partial sweep full parser parity.\\n+Unknown classification stays visible and cannot silently become supported or\\n+excluded. Full grammar parity, file-reading CLI, parser integration into the VM,\\n+and the complete design-259 port remain later milestones.\\ndiff --git a/prototypes/parser/README.md b/prototypes/parser/README.md\\nindex 69547659..2dc87151 100644\\n--- a/prototypes/parser/README.md\\n+++ b/prototypes/parser/README.md\\n@@ -32,10 +32,30 @@ parser application are later steps.\\n \\n The test dump exposes arena structure and locations so tests can check tree\\n shape, ordering, reachability, spans and storage invariants. It is not the\\n-canonical Python AST dump. After this foundation is working, a canonical\\n-renderer and classified top-level examples corpus will drive the parser\\n-differential. Known semantic differences in the mini-VM's M17 ledger do not\\n-authorize AST mismatches.\\n+canonical Python AST dump. M19 (SL-302) adds a separate canonical renderer and\\n+examples inventory; its design is [M19_PARSER_DIFFERENTIAL.md](../minivm/M19_PARSER_DIFFERENTIAL.md).\\n+Known semantic differences in the mini-VM's M17 ledger do not authorize AST\\n+mismatches.\\n+\\n+`canonical_ast(tree: &AstTree) -> Result<String, AstError>` renders a\\n+parser-produced arena using the parse-only Python dump format. It borrows the\\n+tree and returns an owned string with no trailing newline. The explicit\\n+traversal stack preserves M18's depth limit under the VM. It does not validate\\n+arbitrary caller-fabricated arenas.\\n+\\n+The canonical format omits locations and arena IDs, collapses parameter/type\\n+nodes into function headers, and renders integer values in decimal without\\n+suffixes. The arena dump remains necessary to verify those syntax details.\\n+String payloads retain control bytes; only double quotes are escaped, matching\\n+the existing Python writer. Framed test output uses lengths and byte values so\\n+embedded newlines and NUL bytes remain unambiguous.\\n+\\n+The current canonical schema only represents calls with an identifier callee.\\n+A parsed call on another expression returns a located renderer error; the\\n+parser still preserves that call correctly. Grouped identifier calls can render,\\n+but the Python parser currently misparses them (SL-73). These are explicit\\n+diagnostic comparison cases, never tolerated agreement. Full canonical parser\\n+parity depends on resolving grammar debt as well as expanding the subset.\\n \\n The index representation follows the September 10 prototype ruling and\\n supersedes design 259 U2's earlier Box-linked storage choice. Design 259's\\n@@ -69,3 +89,60 @@ new enclosing expression is constructed, its span includes the consumed\\n grouping tokens. An omitted return type is represented by a synthetic Void\\n NamedType with an empty span at the body opener. Integer text is the lexer's\\n normalized number followed by its suffix; String text is decoded content.\\n+\\n+## Canonical comparison and examples inventory\\n+\\n+With the compiler's Python environment active, run the focused renderer gate:\\n+\\n+```sh\\n+python prototypes/parser/test_canonical.py --binary .build/minivm/minivm\\n+python -m unittest discover -s prototypes/parser/tests -p 'test_*.py'\\n+```\\n+\\n+The renderer gate passed 15 cases across VM, LLVM O0/O2, ASan and production\\n+sawc, with identical complete output. Nine cases also matched Python's\\n+parse-only oracle. Four depth/long-chain cases and two grouped/general-callee\\n+cases have independently authored expectations; they do not count as Python\\n+agreement. A separate arena VM run checks structural invariants. The combined\\n+Python harness suite contains 35 passing tests.\\n+\\n+The [inventory report](examples_inventory.md) and [snapshot](examples_inventory.json)\\n+cover all tracked examples, including nested directories. The snapshot records\\n+source hashes, syntax evidence and test expectations. A semantic EXPECT-error\\n+directive does not exclude a file from parser comparison.\\n+\\n+The checked-in JSON uses lossless schema v2 with named columns and shared string\\n+tables to fit sawtracker's request limit. Its `schema` field names every column\\n+and code table; `inventory.decode_snapshot()` reconstructs the full per-file\\n+records. Detailed comparison artifacts retain ordinary object-shaped JSON.\\n+\\n+```sh\\n+python prototypes/parser/inventory.py --check\\n+python prototypes/parser/compare_examples.py --binary .build/minivm/minivm\\n+```\\n+\\n+The snapshot check fails on added/deleted files, changed source or changed\\n+classifications. Run `inventory.py` without `--check` to regenerate and review\\n+both snapshot files. The comparison command independently rebuilds and saves\\n+the current inventory, then tests every candidate in bounded embedded-source\\n+batches. It can measure a changed corpus before the snapshot is updated; its\\n+source hashes additionally detect edits during the run. Snapshot freshness is\\n+a separate submission gate, not a frozen filename allowlist.\\n+\\n+The first sweep passed all 58 candidates (36 top-level, 22 nested), including\\n+29 semantic-negative programs. Of 2,696 tracked examples, 2,536 have unsupported\\n+syntax, 95 produce Python parse errors, and 7 remain unresolved. Those groups\\n+have not established parser parity and are not counted as agreement. Candidates\\n+are selected independently of the prototype result; a refusal or mismatch\\n+fails the comparison rather than changing the classification.\\n+\\n+Use `--artifacts PATH` with a new or empty directory to preserve the inventory,\\n+per-file sources and canonical outputs, batch sources, commands and failure\\n+diagnostics. The comparison parses example source text; it does not typecheck\\n+or execute the example programs. The focused renderer gate checks the same\\n+Saw implementation across execution engines.\\n+\\n+`test_canonical.py --binary .build/minivm/minivm --debt-probe` runs the strict\\n+SL-73 grouped-callee comparison separately. It currently fails on Python's\\n+wrong tree, and will succeed when both parsers agree. It is not part of the\\n+passing fixture set and has no tolerated mismatch entry.\\ndiff --git a/prototypes/parser/canonical_driver.saw b/prototypes/parser/canonical_driver.saw\\nnew file mode 100644\\nindex 00000000..7dab2d3b\\n--- /dev/null\\n+++ b/prototypes/parser/canonical_driver.saw\\n@@ -0,0 +1,36 @@\\n+func dump_canonical_bytes(label: String, value: String) {\\n+    print(label)\\n+    print(value.len())\\n+    var i = 0\\n+    while i < value.len() {\\n+        print(value.byte_at(i) as Int)\\n+        i += 1\\n+    }\\n+}\\n+\\n+func dump_canonical_error(kind: String, error: AstError) {\\n+    print(kind)\\n+    print(\\\"LINE\\\")\\n+    print(error.line)\\n+    print(\\\"COL\\\")\\n+    print(error.col)\\n+    dump_canonical_bytes(\\\"MESSAGE\\\", error.message)\\n+}\\n+\\n+func dump_canonical_case(case_id: Int, source: String) {\\n+    print(\\\"CASE\\\")\\n+    print(case_id)\\n+    match parse_ast(source) {\\n+        case Err(error) -> { dump_canonical_error(\\\"RENDER-ERROR\\\", error) },\\n+                case Ok(value) -> {\\n+                    print(\\\"OK\\\")\\n+                    dump_canonical_bytes(\\\"CANONICAL\\\", value)\\n+                }\\n+            }\\n+        }\\n+    }\\n+    print(\\\"END-CASE\\\")\\n+}\\ndiff --git a/prototypes/parser/compare_examples.py python3\\n+\\\"\\\"\\\"Compare every fresh M19 inventory candidate with the prototype renderer.\\\"\\\"\\\"\\n+\\n+from __future__ import annotations\\n+\\n+import argparse\\n+import hashlib\\n+import json\\n+from pathlib import Path\\n+import re\\n+import subprocess\\n+import sys\\n+import time\\n+from typing import Any\\n+\\n+sys.path.insert(0, str(Path(__file__).resolve().parent))\\n+import inventory\\n+import test_canonical\\n+\\n+\\n+HERE = Path(__file__).resolve().parent\\n+REPO = HERE.parents[1]\\n+PYTHON_DUMP = REPO / \\\"tools/dump_ast.py\\\"\\n+\\n+\\n+def safe_id(relative: str, digest: str) -> str:\\n+    stem = re.sub(r\\\"[^A-Za-z0-9]+\\\", \\\"-\\\", relative).strip(\\\"-\\\")\\n+    return f\\\"{stem}-{digest[:12]}\\\"\\n+\\n+\\n+def write_json(path: Path, value: Any) -> None:\\n+    path.write_text(json.dumps(value, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) + \\\"\\\\n\\\", encoding=\\\"utf-8\\\")\\n+\\n+\\n+def python_oracle(source: bytes, case_dir: Path, timeout: float\\n+
